scope: Offline provider identity diagnostics and same-response cost recovery

boundary_cases: HTTP200 invalid identity with zero native cost settles zero and still rejects
HTTP200 invalid identity with fractional nanoUSD cost preserves upward rounding and rejects
HTTP200 invalid identity with settlement exception attempts settlement once, retains uncertainty and original router_identity failure
HTTP201 invalid identity and valid cost remains uncertain
HTTP202 invalid identity and valid cost remains uncertain
HTTP200 error envelope and valid cost remains uncertain
HTTP200 invalid identity with out-of-range cost remains uncertain
validation.boundary_test_method: Independent inline synthetic injected fetch responses and in-memory accounting; no added application test file or real network request
validation.all_boundary_cases: One injected POST per invocation, rejection retained, no duplicate settlement, no accepted identity metadata, no synthetic secret marker in terminal event

findings.initial_defect: Native cost extraction did not enforce the documented HTTP200-only boundary. Independent HTTP201 reproduction settled1000000nanoUSD despite identity rejection; the same response.ok path also admitted202 for extraction.
findings.correction: nativeOpenRouterCost now requires response.status===200; author added201/202 regressions and independent checks confirm both remain uncertain.
findings.strict_identity: Original Anthropic/model/routing/cache/BYOK/attempt enforcement remains rejecting. First-failed field diagnostics return finite constants rather than raw values.
findings.cost_separation: Validated native cost is kept in openrouter_cost independently of accepted identity metadata. Identity or content failure still rejects and preserves its original classification.
findings.failure_accounting: Missing, invalid, error-envelope and non200 costs remain uncertain; no new failure-path generation lookup or provider retry; at-most-one settlement attempt.
findings.profile_binding: Identity helper, finite field list, billing policy and provider execution are bound into the updated OpenRouter profile; semantic profile unchanged.

historical_integrity.active_application_edits: Intentional new uncommitted version; old frozen manifest cannot be reused for live execution

public_documentation.finding: Vendor documentation defines usage.cost as the account charge and distinguishes upstream provider inference cost.
Opted-in router metadata accompanies successful completion responses, including the Messages route, for routing and cost attribution.

limitations: Accepting same-response usage.cost independently of identity validity is an explicit internal monitoring trust policy for the fixed OpenRouter POST, not invoice finality or a hard billing guarantee.
The exact M30 identity field and actual failed-attempt cost remain unresolved; synthetic evidence cannot retrospectively settle that charge.
No live provider reliability, three-case website success, release readiness or production acceptance is demonstrated.
Mandatory trace-callback exception behavior is preserved rather than redesigned.
Only the four named application files were reviewed; unrelated operational edits are outside this verdict.
